ABOUT ME

Yidan Nai is a London-based product designer and interdisciplinary creator currently studying MA Design for Industry 5.0 at Central Saint Martins, University of the Arts London. Her practice focuses on intelligent hardware, embodied intelligence, robotics, wearable technology and human-computer interaction, exploring how emerging technologies can become products and services with genuine utility, thoughtful experiences and social value.

Her projects span wearable flexible sensing systems for prosthetic users, intelligent water-rescue equipment, AI home-agriculture robots, ergonomic products, Alzheimer’s care systems and inclusive interactive art installations. This experience has shaped a working method grounded in user needs and technical validation, while balancing product experience, engineering feasibility and future commercial value.

Technically, she works with Arduino, sensor systems, foundational programming, 3D printing and digital fabrication, integrating sound, light, movement, haptic feedback and real-time data visualisation into interactive experiences. She also uses Rhino, Blender, Figma, Clo3D and TouchDesigner for complex surface modelling, product and wearable prototyping, interface design and motion-based visual communication, while continuing to explore AI agents, computer vision and large language models in consumer intelligent products.
